main_text.p: laret : sed vel maxime, quod Philosophiam dignam iudicarem, in qua exornanda & expolienda omnes ingenii nervos contenderem. Semper enim cum docta & veneranda Antiquitate in hac sua sententia, Philosophiam singulare Dei donum esse, eiusque studium non solum esse iucundum, & liberali homine dignum; verumetiam ad sapientiam &prudentiam, quæ duæ sunt præcipuæ intellectus humani virtutes & quasi lumina, comparandam apprime vtile & necessarium: Ac licet negari non possit, illam à compluribus partim barbariei cæno esse inquinatam, partim subtilium & inanum disputationum spinis intricatam, partim falsorum aut saltem incertorum dogmatum tenebris obscuratam, partim denique ab vsu turpi & nefando conculcatam; tamen quæ vitio hominum fiunt, illa non æquum esse duxi, ut ipsi Philoso-

page.notes: Page number "6" at the lower left is doubtful; it may be a signature or ornament. The text ends mid-word at "Philoso-" and continues on the next page as "phiæ", which is also the catchword. Italic boundaries inside the text are read from the scan and may be slightly off. The "s" long s has been written as s, and "ƈt" as "ct". Grey blurred text at the lower right is a digitiser's banner and was left out.
